extracted.intended_audience: public relations/communications professionals drafting new-hire or executive appointment press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for writing a press release announcing a new hire or executive appointment, covering structure, headline, body content, quotes, multimedia, length, boilerplate, and exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard structure: Logo and contact info
rubrics_metrics.description: Include logo and contact info as part of the standard press-release structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-of-release elements; contact info enables media follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard structure: Release date
rubrics_metrics.description: Display the release date prominently in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the dateline/release date to indicate when the announcement is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard structure: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise headline that summarizes the announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline requirements are specified separately (see Headline Requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard structure: Location/dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the location/dateline near the top of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides geographic context for the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard structure: Body
rubrics_metrics.description: The main text of the release containing the announcement details, organized into a first paragraph and subsequent paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Body guidance includes what to cover in the first paragraph and subsequent paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard structure: Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: A short company description in a standard format included at the end of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Boilerplate rubric: 30-100 word company description, standard format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline requirement: Full name of new hire
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the full name of the new hire in the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps searchability and immediate identification of the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline requirement: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the new hire's title in the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveys the level/scope of the role at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline requirement: Company name
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the company name in the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures the announcement is clearly associated with the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline requirement: Strong verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use strong verbs such as 'welcomes,' 'appoints,' or 'announces' in the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbs should convey action and clarity about the nature of the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline requirement: Under 15 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the headline under 15 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brevity improves readability and media pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline requirement: Clear and informative
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the headline clear and informative, avoiding vagueness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline should communicate who, what, and role without needing to read the body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Example headlines provided by the guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Acme Corp Appoints Jane Smith as Chief Marketing Officer'; 'TechFirm Welcomes Dr. John Doe as Head of AI Research'. Use as models for structure and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: First paragraph: Full name
rubrics_metrics.description: First paragraph must include the full name of the new hire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load identifying information so readers immediately know who the release is about.

rubrics_metrics.name: First paragraph: Job title
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the new hire's job title in the first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces the headline and clarifies role responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: First paragraph: Relevant background
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the new hire's relevant background in the first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the summary focused on experiences most pertinent to the new role.

rubrics_metrics.name: First paragraph: How expertise aligns with company goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain briefly how the executive's expertise aligns with company goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide strategic context so the hire appears purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: First paragraph: What they bring to the team
rubrics_metrics.description: State what the new hire brings to the team in terms of skills/value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about contributions (leadership, technical skills, market experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent paragraphs: length (50-200 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent paragraphs should run roughly 50-200 words in total for detail expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these paragraphs to expand on expertise and accomplishments without becoming verbose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent paragraphs: Detailed expertise and accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide more detailed descriptions of the executive's expertise and accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete examples and outcomes to substantiate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent paragraphs: Career highlights
rubrics_metrics.description: List career highlights that are relevant to the new role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on milestones that demonstrate leadership, growth, or domain authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent paragraphs: Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Include education details where relevant to the role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention degrees/certifications that lend credibility to the hire's expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent paragraphs: Notable previous companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Name notable prior employers to establish pedigree and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing recognized organizations can help media and readers contextualize the hire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent paragraphs: Awards/recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Include awards or recognition that support the executive's qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite notable honors that are directly relevant to the role or industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent paragraphs: How hire expands or strengthens business
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the hire expands or strengthens the company's business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie the individual's background to tangible business needs or opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes: new executive
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quote from the new executive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The executive's quote should reflect enthusiasm, vision, or perspective that humanizes the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes: senior leader
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quote from a senior leader (CEO, board chair) about strategic value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quote should position the hire within company strategy and convey leadership endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length: overall ideal (400-500 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for 400-500 words for a standard new-hire press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This length balances completeness and newsroom/readership attention spans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length: up to 600 words for major executive
rubrics_metrics.description: For major executive hires, the release can extend up to 600 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow more space for expanded background and strategic context for high-profile roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia: professional headshot (essential)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a professional headshot — listed as essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality image supports media use and online distribution; required for most outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia: team photo (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: A team photo is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only if it adds relevant context and is high-quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia: company logo
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the company logo with the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Branding helps recognition in syndication and social sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia: introductory video (for major hires)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an introductory video for major hires when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video can increase engagement for high-profile announcements; use professionally produced clips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: 30-100 word company description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a 30-100 word company description in a standard boilerplate format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep boilerplate current and consistent across releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: What not to include: personal life details
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include personal life details in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep focus on professional qualifications and role-related information.

rubrics_metrics.name: What not to include: compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid disclosing compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary or package details are inappropriate for standard press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: What not to include: reasons for previous departure
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include reasons for previous departure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid potentially sensitive or negative background details; keep tone forward-looking.

rubrics_metrics.name: What not to include: speculation about strategic direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not speculate about future strategic direction in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid promises or speculation that could be construed as forward guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: What not to include: promises about future actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make promises about future actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep statements factual and avoid commitments that could create expectations or legal exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: full name and exact title
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the release contains the full name and exact title of the hire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces identity and role precision; duplicates headline/first-paragraph requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: specific previous role and employer
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference the hire's specific previous role and employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides credibility and context about the candidate's background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: years of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Include years of experience where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies seniority and domain tenure; include only when it adds clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: quantifiable achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: List quantifiable achievements (revenue grown, team built, products launched).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific metrics or outcomes to substantiate claims rather than vague praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: strategic context
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why this hire fits company strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie individual capabilities to company objectives to make the hire newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: two quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide two quotes: one from the new hire and one from a senior leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Quotes rubric; both quotes together strengthen narrative and endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: education credentials (if relevant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include educational credentials when relevant to the role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include degrees/certifications that materially support the hire's qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: reporting structure (if changed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note reporting structure changes if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies organizational impact (e.g., who the new hire reports to).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: start date
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the hire's start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State start date to inform stakeholders and media about timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: headshot included
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that a headshot is included with the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matches Multimedia/headshot requirement; essential for media use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: boilerplate current
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the boilerplate is current and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid outdated descriptive language or old facts in the boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: AP style throughout
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AP (Associated Press) style throughout the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhering to AP style enhances media friendliness and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: no promotional fluff
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid promotional fluff and marketing-heavy language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep tone informational and professional rather than overtly promotional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: distinctive (not generic announcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the announcement distinctive rather than a generic template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific, newsworthy details to differentiate the release and increase pickup.
